title: Delos
summary: Delos is one of the smallest Cyclades islands, an ancient religious, political and commercial centre of the Aegean, traditionally the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis. Inhabited from the late 3rd millennium bce, it hosted the Delian Confederacy in 478 bce, became a Roman free port after 166 bce, and declined commercially by the end of the 1st century ce.

reviewer_note: The start year (-2299) is an approximation of the 'late 3rd millennium bce' and the end year (100) approximates the end of the 1st century ce. The MANTO source covers mythology and gives no dates. Britannica says the island remained almost uninhabited after 42 bce, which is why the end date is a rough marker of commercial decline.
